clue.text: Dictator hated for ill-treatment

indicators.note: ill-treatment is rough handling, so the letters before it are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tyrant loathed because of the way he abused people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-treatment' looks like one word, but 'ill' is the last piece of fodder and 'treatment' is the anagram signal working on HATED FOR ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazi leader is the archetypal twentieth-century dictator, holding absolute power over Germany.

clue.text: Cut off a weed

explanation.surface: A gardener lops a weed.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock a tail is to cut it short, and dock is also a common broad-leaved weed of the genus Rumex.

clue.text: They may part with a smile

definitions.text: They may part with a smile

parts.words: They may part with a smile
parts.note: not people separating cheerfully but the parts of the face that open when someone grins

explanation.surface: Friends who say goodbye cheerfully.
explanation.definitionFit: When you smile your mouth opens, so the two fleshy edges of the mouth move apart.

clue.text: Worker given guidance is touched

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as on a farm or a ship
led means guided, shown the way

explanation.surface: An employee who has been steered along feels emotionally moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' just links the wordplay to the definition 'touched', meaning felt with the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handled has been felt or held with the hands, which is to say physically touched.

clue.text: System for better transport

explanation.surface: A gambler's method and a way of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'better' here is someone who bets; the tote is the totalisator, the pool betting system at British racecourses.
explanation.definitionFit: The tote is a pool-betting system for punters, and to tote something is to carry or haul it.

clue.text: Had tree replaced, safe from lightning

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different place, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone moved a tree so it would not attract lightning strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical installation connected to the ground is protected, since a strike's current runs harmlessly away.

clue.text: The lowest figure, fractionally, even if quite common

definitions.text: The lowest figure, fractionally, even if quite common

parts.words: The lowest figure, fractionally, even if quite common
parts.note: in a fraction the bottom number is this, and the phrase 'lowest common' one is a familiar maths term

explanation.surface: A remark about the least impressive person, who is rather vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fraction, the number written below the line is this term, as in 'lowest common' version.

clue.text: Dramatist keeps a share — quite wrongly

indicators.note: quite wrongly says the letters before it are put in an entirely incorrect order

explanation.surface: A playwright holds on to a stake in a theatre without any right to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bard of Stratford is the most celebrated English playwright, author of Hamlet and King Lear.

clue.text: Son of Adam said to sound archaic

indicators.note: says the word that fills in for 'said' is heard in its old-fashioned form, and the answer is pronounced the same

parts.note: saith is the old biblical form of the verb meaning says

explanation.surface: A claim that a biblical figure's name has an old-world ring.
explanation.walkthrough: SAITH, as in 'thus saith the Lord', is pronounced like the name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam and Eve's third son was born after the death of Abel.

clue.text: Remedial needlework

parts.note: not mending clothes but a healing therapy that is worked with needles

explanation.surface: Sewing that repairs damaged clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese therapy treats ailments by inserting fine needles at points on the body.

clue.text: Captain's favourable report on Commanding Officer

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the report follows the officer

parts.note: OK is an approving verdict, all correct

explanation.surface: A ship's master gets a good write-up about his senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the explorer Captain James Cook; the 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: James Cook was the eighteenth-century naval officer who charted the Pacific, always called Captain.

clue.text: Teenagers make fuss over the French perfumes

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother
le is French for the
scents are perfumes

explanation.surface: Young people kick up a row about French fragrances.
explanation.definitionFit: Young people between childhood and adulthood are in their teens, the stage of adolescence.

clue.text: Clause in insurance policy motorists will try to avoid

explanation.surface: A line in a car insurance document that drivers dread.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, a driving offence earns an endorsement: penalty points recorded on the licence.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer adds a clause amending cover, and a court adds penalty points to a driving licence.

clue.text: Meant not to be found in action

indicators.note: says the word before sits inside the next piece

parts.note: a deed is an act or action

explanation.surface: Something intended but never seen in practice.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to signify, so a word that denoted something meant it.

clue.text: Bed for many a Russian

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number
Ivan is a typical Russian man's name

explanation.surface: Sleeping space for lots of people from Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A low backless couch that doubles as a sofa and a bed.

clue.text: Mother checks out but doesn't leave

indicators.note: out here means outside, the checks enclosing mother

parts.note: reins in means checks or restrains, as reins do a horse
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Mum looks over the hotel bill yet stays on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checks out' looks like a hotel departure, the opposite of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay put, so someone who does not leave stays where they are.

clue.text: Drums in lively dances

explanation.surface: Percussion accompanying spirited folk dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a spool or drum for winding cable, and also a fast Scottish or Irish dance.

clue.text: Took a chance and got the chop

explanation.surface: Someone gambled and was sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicing is gambling with dice, and diced food has been chopped into small cubes.

clue.text: Main shareholder?

parts.note: not a major investor but the beast with a mane that takes the biggest portion, the proverbial share

explanation.surface: A question about who owns most of a company.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion's share is the largest portion, and the big cat has a mane, which sounds like main.

clue.text: Wrath possibly shown by head

explanation.surface: Anger displayed by a boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Wrath is the north-western tip of mainland Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Wrath is one such promontory, and a head or headland is a promontory jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Check out of Kabul

indicators.note: out of here means put out of order, so the city's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A security inspection on leaving the Afghan capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To baulk someone is to thwart or check them, and a baulk is a hindrance.

clue.text: A large number put the charge on account

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the charge goes below the account in this down entry

parts.note: a bill is an account of what is owed
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A huge sum results from putting the fee on someone's tab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means placed after, so the charge follows the account; in this down clue it sits below it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand million is a very large figure.

clue.text: His mark was made in India

indicators.note: was made says these letters are manufactured into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A man made his name on the subcontinent.
explanation.definitionFit: This Himalayan region lies in the north of India, its territory disputed with Pakistan.

clue.text: Support us in shame

indicators.note: in places the word before inside the next one

parts.note: a stain is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: A plea for help in a time of disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to bear its weight or keep it going, to support it.

clue.text: Enjoy embracing one's rescuer

parts.note: to savour is to enjoy
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is part of the possessive

explanation.surface: Relishing a hug from the person who saved you.
explanation.definitionFit: A saviour is someone who saves another from danger.

clue.text: Trees in Wilhelmstrasse

indicators.note: in says the answer is concealed inside the street name

explanation.surface: Trees growing in a famous Berlin street.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a tall deciduous tree, so trees is a plural example.

clue.text: A tree for future scrutiny, perhaps

explanation.surface: A tree examined to see what lies ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm is a tropical tree, and a fortune-teller reads the palm of the hand to predict the future.

clue.text: Courage needed on icy roads

explanation.surface: Bravery needed when driving in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is pluck or determination, and grit is also the crushed stone spread on frozen roads.

clue.text: He goes down or rises in play

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word is backwards

explanation.surface: An actor who falls or rises in the drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes down' places HE at the top of this down entry; the definition is the central character in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal male character in a play or story is its leading figure.

clue.text: Novel form of alarm — sirens

indicators.note: form of says the letters are given a new shape

explanation.surface: A new kind of alarm made of sirens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new', but it is the definition: George Eliot's novel about a weaver.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's 1861 story of a reclusive weaver is a classic Victorian novel.

clue.text: Have an inclination to be a nurse

explanation.surface: Feeling drawn to a caring profession.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend is to be inclined, and to tend the sick is to nurse them.

clue.text: Mountaineer out for the count

indicators.note: out says the letters before it are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A climber is knocked out in a boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out for the count' is a boxing knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting things one by one is an act of listing and numbering, a tally.
